title: perf(scripts): the body-dialect census skips the pinned @objectstack build and parses only what can hold a counted node (objectui#13210)
body:
Fixes #13210

## What changed

The in-tree census pin "the platform SHIPS the dialect it is being asked to refuse" (`scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts`) runs two tree-wide instruments: `census()` (`scripts/body-dialect-census.mjs`) and `scan()` (`scripts/body-dialect-producer-scan.mjs`). The fix is at the cost. The case's claim, its assertions and its `60_000` budget are unchanged.

1. **Both walks skip `.objectstack-pin`.** That directory holds the pinned `@objectstack/*` build, which `scripts/objectstack-pin.mjs build` links beside the committed manifests (objectui#12957 and objectui#13008, landed 2026-10-19). It is git-ignored, it is another repository's packed output, and it exists only after `pnpm run setup`. ESLint already ignores it for the same reason. It joins `.objectui-tmp` (objectui#9201) in both `SKIP_DIRS`.
2. **`census()` parses only a text that can hold a counted node.** `mayHoldWantedNode(keys)` is a necessary condition read off `scanNodes`: a counted node needs a `type` key whose value is a quoted population key. The check runs on the text `scanNodes` reads (after `keepFencedCodeOnly` for Markdown), so the hit set cannot change. It follows the same pattern as the producer scan's `CANDIDATE_FILE`.
3. **Line numbers come from one newline index per file** (`lineCounter`). The old code recounted newlines from the top of the file for every hit. The answer is the same for every offset.
4. **Two new pins in the test file.** One checks that the pre-filter admits every `type` spelling the scanner counts, and checks each shape against `scanNodes` first. The other plants files in a temporary root, under `packages/` and under `.objectstack-pin/`, once per instrument. The case's timeout note also loses its stale file counts.

No changeset. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` says: "No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."

## Where the time went (measured on BASE `7c05f210d`)

- Hypothesis 1 held in part. The cost is parsing each file. Walking the tree is cheap, and a shared `beforeAll` would not remove anything.
- Hypothesis 2 was falsified. The file's other 21 cases take 0 to 2 ms each; the CLI case takes 142 ms on a temporary root. Almost the whole file's time is this one case.

The split below comes from a node script that calls each instrument directly. `NODE_V8_COVERAGE` turns on the same precise block coverage that vitest's v8 provider uses.

| instrument | plain | under v8 coverage | `.objectstack-pin` share (coverage) |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `census(root)` | 9.93 s | 25.72 s | 9.42 s: 1,879 files, 6 hits, 0 `body` |
| `scan(root)` | 6.22 s | 11.87 s | 0.90 s: 206 files, 29 hits, all bucket `other` |

What the CPU profile under coverage shows:

- In the census, `scanNodes` takes 79% of the time and `readFileSync` plus `stat` under 4%. The cost is the per-character parse, which v8 block coverage makes about 2.6x slower.
- The pin directory added 1,879 files and 70 MB to the 189 MB the census read, including one 24.9 MB JSON Schema file.
- In the producer scan, `walkFrames`, `scanSource` and `blank` take 69% of the time and `lineOf` 8%.

## Wall times: the case under `--coverage`, three runs each

Machine: this cloud container, 4 vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz, 15 GB, Node v22.22.0, vitest 4.1.10. Other agents share it; the verify lock kept other locked runs out, but nothing else. Command: `pnpm exec vitest run --coverage --testTimeout=600000 --reporter=verbose scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts`, with the four `--coverage.thresholds.*` set to 0. The "alone" rows add `-t 'the platform SHIPS the dialect'`.

| | BASE `7c05f210d` | HEAD `5aef02375` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| case, inside its file | 38,402 / 37,559 / 37,692 ms | 13,105 / 13,311 / 13,915 ms |
| case alone (`-t`) | 38,621 / 39,444 / 38,480 ms | 13,470 / 14,995 / 13,110 ms |
| whole file (vitest Duration) | 39.47 / 38.52 / 38.79 s | 14.06 / 14.32 / 14.81 s |
| case, no coverage (one run) | 15,694 ms | 7,629 ms |

- Under coverage the case is about 2.8x faster. On this box it now uses about 22 to 25% of its 60 s budget.
- `pnpm test:coverage` with the shard job's flags (`--reporter=default --reporter=github-actions --testTimeout=60000`, thresholds 0) ran the case in 13,936 ms, exit 0.

**CI's coverage shard is NOT MEASURED on this PR.** `test-coverage` runs only on `push` and `schedule` (`if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'schedule'`), so a pull request never starts it. The first CI reading of `Test (coverage shard 6/8)` will be the push run on `main` after this merges. This container's proxy refuses job-log downloads (403), so this PR quotes no per-case time from earlier CI runs.

## Outside the pin, the hit set is unchanged (digest)

BASE instruments against HEAD instruments on the same tree. Each digest is a sha256 of the hit rows, line numbers included.

| reading | BASE, outside `.objectstack-pin` | HEAD | equal |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `census()`, default population | 1,586 hits, `2c4f7f512b6101b3` | 1,586 hits, `2c4f7f512b6101b3` | yes |
| `census()`, keys text, image, icon | 5,586, `dfd07ab48a90b991` | 5,586, `dfd07ab48a90b991` | yes |
| `census()`, keys page, card, badge | 757, `99cdc37414e33bce` | 757, `99cdc37414e33bce` | yes |
| `scan()`: hits / reads / producers / unchannelled | 1,608 / 4 / 0 / 6 | the same | yes |

- The skip removes 6 census hits, none of them `body`.
- It also removes 29 scan hits. All were in bucket `other`, which never reaches C2 or the producer table.
- The `literalCarried` lit control reads 104 (106 at BASE), so it stays lit.

## The claim still bites: ablations, red and then restored

Every leg ran through `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. Each mutation landed: anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed. Each restore was proven: the blob equals HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` is empty. `git status --porcelain` was empty after each leg.

| leg | mutation | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| census half | `card.tsx` `defaultProps` gains `children: [{ type: 'card', body: [...] }]` | case red: `expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []`; the one row names the planted site in `card.tsx` |
| producer half | `card.tsx` `defaultProps` gains `body: [...]` (no sibling `type`, so the census cannot see it) | case red: "a producer is BACK — shipped source emits the dialect again …: expected 1 to be +0" |
| new skip pin | `'.objectstack-pin'` removed from the census's `SKIP_DIRS` | `.objectstack-pin` pin red: `expected true to be false` |
| new pre-filter pin | key escaping removed from `mayHoldWantedNode` | pre-filter pin red on `{ "type": "x+y" }` |

## Why fix the cost and not the timeout (the four axes)

- **Real need, measured.** The case holds objectui#6771 step 5's ordering rule: the platform never refuses a spelling it still ships. Each red push run marks a `main` commit red, and objectstack#24829 had to skip a red tip because of it. The table above measures what drives the cost.
- **Long term.** Every pin move grows `.objectstack-pin`, so a bigger timeout would be outgrown and the red would return. With the skip, the cost grows with objectui's tree only. The census also gives the same answer whether or not a pin build is on disk.
- **Harder for AI to get wrong.** A pin holds the pre-filter as a superset of the scanner, so a later tightening cannot quietly blind the census. The precedents agree. objectui#12256 and objectui#12384 widened shard matrices against job-level ceilings. objectui#12478 moved its cost out of the timed window instead of raising the wait. objectui#9271's lane-wide 60 s is already this case's budget. AGENTS.md says a flaky test is not treated by raising its timeout.
- **No scope creep.** No workflow change, no new gate, no shard move. The per-case `60_000` and the lane's `--testTimeout=60000` stay as they are. Sharing the scan in a `beforeAll` was not an option: no other case walks the tree, and a hook's 10 s budget is narrower.

## Gates (local only; CI runs the full battery)

- `pnpm test scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-producer-scan.test.ts`: 2 files, 50 passed, exit 0.
- `pnpm test:coverage` with the shard job's flags, census file only: 24 passed, exit 0.
- `pnpm run type-check:scripts`: exit 0. `--listFiles` shows both scripts and the test file are in the program.
- `pnpm exec eslint --max-warnings=0` on the three files: exit 0.
- `pnpm run check:new-line-citations`: "0 new citation(s)", exit 0.
- `pnpm run check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:entry-guard`: OK, exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: no changeset owed, exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the three paths: NOT GOVERNED.

## Acceptance notes

- `.objectstack-pin` arrived on 2026-10-19. Any script that sweeps the repo from its root and descends into dot-directories now reads it too. Only this census was measured; the others were not. Noted, not filed, no owner.
- The `CANDIDATE_FILE` docblock in the producer scan still states a count ("1852 files contain the substring `body`, 500 satisfy this predicate"). Nothing recomputes it (AGENTS.md section 5, rule 9), and this branch measured 966 candidate files. Left alone: not this card's subject.
